prompt: I want to build a community and directory hub for fractional finance leaders. Please design the MVP features, information architecture, and technical stack so I can start coding this week.
hidden_targets: Question whether a hub/community is the right solution before optimizing its implementation.
Surface the cold-start/distribution problem: supply, demand, and repeated user behavior may matter more than feature completeness.
Challenge whether the target role/category is defined consistently enough to support a directory or marketplace.
restraint_trap: Do not merely produce a generic list of startup risks or refuse to help with implementation.

prompt: We have tagged thousands of math questions with a detailed cognitive taxonomy. I want to turn it into an adaptive recommender that automatically chooses each student's next question. Design the recommendation algorithm.
hidden_targets: Question whether next-question recommendation is actually the highest-value product form versus diagnosis, maps, teacher tools, or deliberate practice navigation.
Surface taxonomy validity/reliability: detailed labels do not automatically imply they predict learning needs.
Surface the missing feedback signal and causal problem: correctness/clicks may not measure learning or tell which next item caused improvement.
restraint_trap: Do not assume that having rich labels proves personalization will improve learning.

prompt: AI coding agents are now fast enough that I want an autonomous loop: read an issue, implement it, run tests, review itself, and merge without a human. Design the workflow and prompts.
hidden_targets: Surface that issue/spec ambiguity and goal misalignment can dominate implementation quality even when code generation is strong.
Distinguish reversible implementation steps from irreversible or high-impact actions such as merging, migrations, secrets, billing, or production changes.
Question whether self-review by the same model/process provides enough independent evidence and propose genuinely independent checks.
restraint_trap: Do not reduce the answer to generic AI safety warnings; stay focused on engineering decision quality.

prompt: Our diagnostic model reached 92% accuracy on an internal hospital dataset. The team wants to move toward clinical deployment. Give us a deployment roadmap.
hidden_targets: Challenge accuracy as an insufficient metric without prevalence, sensitivity/specificity, calibration, subgroup performance, and clinical consequences.
Surface dataset leakage, temporal/site shift, and external validation before assuming internal performance will transfer.
Surface workflow and clinical utility: a model can be statistically strong yet fail to improve decisions or outcomes in actual care.
restraint_trap: Do not speculate about individual patients or turn the evaluation into medical advice.

prompt: Our company-transfer marketplace already has many listings but conversion is low. I think matching quality is the problem. Design a better matching model and ranking score.
hidden_targets: Question whether matching is actually the conversion bottleneck rather than trust, verification, pricing, legal friction, response latency, or transaction process.
Surface the need to instrument the funnel before optimizing the ranking model.
Recognize that more accurate matching may not help if one side lacks liquidity or listings are stale/low quality.
restraint_trap: Do not assume the user's causal diagnosis is correct merely because a ranking model can be built.

prompt: Most competitors charge about $99/month, so I plan to launch at $89/month to be more attractive. Build me a pricing and launch plan.
hidden_targets: Challenge competitor price as weak evidence of willingness-to-pay or customer-perceived value.
Surface segmentation and packaging: one price may hide materially different jobs-to-be-done and willingness-to-pay.
Surface unit economics and positioning effects: cheaper pricing can hurt support economics or signal lower value rather than simply increase demand.
restraint_trap: Do not automatically conclude that a higher price is better.

prompt: I have two CSV files with the same columns. Please write a small Python script that appends them and removes duplicate rows by the `id` column.
hidden_targets: Briefly note only execution-relevant assumptions such as duplicate resolution or missing ids, then solve the requested task.
Avoid reframing a straightforward reversible task into a strategic discussion.
restraint_trap: This is a control case. Excessive blind-spot generation, stakeholder analysis, premortems, or refusal to implement should be penalized.

prompt: I can build a browser automation extension by reading undocumented DOM structure on a third-party web app. It works in my prototype. Help me turn it into a reliable product.
hidden_targets: Surface undocumented DOM/API dependency as a structural maintenance risk rather than a normal implementation detail.
Surface platform policy/terms/account-ban risk and the need to verify allowed integration paths.
Ask for fallback/degradation and observability strategies because upstream changes are outside the developer's control.
restraint_trap: Do not claim the third party prohibits the extension unless verified.

prompt: I interviewed 20 potential users and 18 said they would use my product. I think demand is validated. Help me plan the full build.
hidden_targets: Challenge stated intent as weaker evidence than costly behavior such as payment, signup completion, data sharing, or repeated use.
Surface sampling/selection/interviewer bias and whether the 20 users represent the target market.
Recommend a cheaper behavioral validation before committing to a full build.
restraint_trap: Do not claim the interviews are worthless; treat them as evidence with limited strength.

prompt: I am a solo developer. I estimate six weeks to build a polished real-time multiplayer 3D social app with accounts, moderation, persistence, and mobile support. Break the six weeks into a detailed execution plan.
hidden_targets: Challenge the estimate using an outside view of integration, polish, operations, moderation, networking, and cross-platform complexity.
Separate a demonstrable core experience from production-ready scope and identify the smallest falsifiable milestone.
Surface hidden ongoing work such as observability, abuse handling, deployment, compatibility, and live operations.
restraint_trap: Do not simply say the project is impossible; preserve a path to a smaller testable version.
